newsitem.title: USA: Army rape case jury has testimony read back.
newsitem.headline: Army rape case jury has testimony read back.

text.p: The military jury in the court-martial rape trial of Staff Sgt. Delmar Simpson began its fourth day of deliberations Monday, reviewing testimony it had sought to hear again.
Army Trial Judge Col. Paul Johnston read the testimony back to the jury, which involved an account of one of the alleged sexual attacks.

Simpson is charged with 19 counts of rape involving six female trainees at the Aberdeen Proving Ground's Ordinance Centre and School and 35 other counts on charges including forceable sodomy, indecent assault and maltreatment.

The six-member panel had requested a review of testimony from the witness on Saturday. The transcript was not available at that time so they broke for the weekend after a total of 16 hours of deliberation over three days last week.

The witness, a confidante of one of the alleged victims, quoted the 20-year-old woman as saying Simpson had restrained her wrists with one hand and undressed her with the other before having sex with her.

"She never said anything about him holding her hand. That's my recollection," Simpson's lawyer Frank Spinner told reporters just after the jury resumed deliberations. "What's puzzling to me is that they didn't ask to hear her testimony."

Simpson, 32, has pleaded guilty to 11 counts of consensual sex and five counts of propositioning, for which he faces a maximum sentence of 32 years in prison. He faces a life sentence if convicted of rape.

His case was the first to go to trial in a major sexual misconduct scandal at the Army's Aberdeen Proving Ground, which broke last November and prompted an Army-wide investigation into sexual harassment.
